title: 65 Affirmation Journal Prompts (With Examples)
description: 65 affirmation journal prompts to write your own encouraging words, plus examples and how to start an affirmation journal. Write yours privately on this page.
intro: **Affirmation journal prompts** help you write your own short, encouraging sentences and actually believe them. Below are 65 prompts for confidence, calm, work, body, relationships and hard days, plus affirmation journal examples and a simple way to start. Write yours in the private diary at the top of this page.

writer.title: My affirmation today
writer.hint: I am... / I can... / I am learning to...

blocks.p: An affirmation is a short, positive sentence you say or write to yourself, like I can handle hard things. An affirmation journal is where you write these sentences, think about why they matter and notice when they start to feel true.

Affirmations are not magic words, and they work best when they feel believable. If I am completely confident feels like a lie, try I am getting more confident each time I speak up. Encouraging self-talk you believe beats a big promise you do not.

blocks.tip: A good affirmation is **short, positive, in the present tense and believable to you**. Adding phrases like I am learning to or I am allowed to can make it easier to accept.

sections.h2: How to start an affirmation journal

steps.name: Notice a harsh thought.
steps.text: Write down one thing you often tell yourself that brings you down, like I always mess things up.

steps.name: Flip it gently.
steps.text: Write a kinder, true version: I make mistakes, and I learn from them.

steps.name: Answer one prompt.
steps.text: Use a prompt below to explore why this affirmation matters and when you need it most.

steps.name: Write it three times.
steps.text: Repeating it in your own handwriting, or typing it, helps it stick.

steps.name: Take it with you.
steps.text: Read it in the morning, on a sticky note or on your phone lock screen.

sections.h2: Affirmation journal prompts to write your own

prompts: What is a mean thing I often say to myself? Rewrite it as a fair, kind affirmation.
What do I most need to believe about myself this week?
Finish this sentence five ways: I am someone who...
Finish this sentence five ways: I am allowed to...
Finish this sentence five ways: I am learning to...
What would someone who loves me want me to remember every day?
What words would have helped me most as a teenager? Write them for me now.
What feeling do I want more of? Write an affirmation that invites it.
Which affirmation feels too big right now? Make a smaller, truer version.
What is one thing about me that is true and good, even on a bad day?
When have I been braver than I expected? What does that say about me?
What is one thing I know I do well? Write it as an I am sentence.
Which situation makes me doubt myself? What would I like to tell myself before it?
What would confident me do differently tomorrow?
Write an affirmation for speaking up in a meeting, class or group.
What compliment have I heard more than once? Turn it into an affirmation.
Which past success can I point to when I feel unsure?
How do I want to carry myself when I walk into a room?
What skill am I proud of building? Write an affirmation about it.
What does it look like to trust myself a little more today?

sections.h2: Affirmation journal prompts for calm and anxious moments

blocks.p: Affirmations can help in tense moments, but they are not a replacement for professional care if anxiety is strong. See [journal prompts for anxiety](/journal-prompts-for-anxiety/) for more support.

prompts: What do I need to hear when my heart is racing?
Write an affirmation I can repeat on a slow out-breath.
What is true about this moment that my worry is ignoring?
Which calming phrase has helped me before?
Write an affirmation that gives me permission to rest.
What can I let be unfinished today? Write an affirmation about it.
How can I remind myself that feelings pass?
Write an affirmation for the night before something I am nervous about.
What do I want to tell my body when it feels tense?
What does safe and steady sound like in words?

sections.h2: Affirmation prompts for work, school and goals

blocks.p: Affirmations pair well with goal setting. For bigger plans, try our [manifestation journal prompts](/manifestation-journal-prompts/).

prompts: What goal am I working on? Write an affirmation about the effort, not just the result.
What do I want to believe about my ability to learn new things?
Write an affirmation for a day when I feel behind.
What value do I bring to my team or class?
How can I speak to myself after a mistake at work?
Write an affirmation that reminds me rest is part of doing good work.
What does progress, not perfection, sound like in one sentence?
Which deadline is stressing me? Write an affirmation that keeps me steady.
What would I say to a coworker who doubts themselves like I do?

sections.h2: Affirmation journal prompts for body, love and relationships

blocks.p: For more on kindness toward yourself, see [self-love journal prompts](/self-love-journal-prompts/).

prompts: Write an affirmation that thanks my body for what it does.
What do I want to believe about how I look, in a way I can accept?
What do I deserve in a friendship or relationship? Write it as an affirmation.
Write an affirmation for setting a boundary kindly.
What kind of love do I want to give myself today?
Write an affirmation for days when I feel lonely.
How can I remind myself I am worth people's time?
Write an affirmation about being enough as I am right now.
What would I tell myself after a disagreement with someone I love?
What is one true, hopeful sentence I can hold onto today?
Write an affirmation that allows me to feel sad without judging myself.
What hard time have I already come through? Write an affirmation from it.
What can I promise myself for the next hour?
Write an affirmation for starting again tomorrow.
What would I write on a card to myself if I were in the hospital or sick in bed?
Write an affirmation that reminds me I do not have to do this alone.
Which of today's affirmations feels most true right now? Why?
Pick my favorite affirmation from this page and write when I will read it this week.
Write a short list of affirmations to save for my next bad day.
What will I say to myself the next time I notice my inner critic?
Look back at affirmations I wrote a month ago. Which ones feel more true now?
What is my affirmation for this whole year?
Write an affirmation that I would want someone I love to say to themselves.
If I could only keep one affirmation forever, which would it be?
How did I feel before writing today, and how do I feel now?
Write a closing line to end today's entry with calm.

blocks.p: Here is how an entry can turn a harsh thought into encouraging self-talk.

example.label: Affirmation journal example
example.title: My affirmation today
example.text:
Harsh thought: I'm terrible at presentations.
Truer version: I get nervous, and I still get through it.
Affirmation: I am prepared, and I can speak clearly.
Why: I practiced twice and know my slides.
I am prepared, and I can speak clearly.
I am prepared, and I can speak clearly.

ul: I can handle one thing at a time.
I am allowed to rest without earning it.
I am learning, and learning takes time.
My feelings are real, and they will pass.
I bring something good to the people around me.
I am doing my best with what I have today.
I can be kind to myself and still grow.
I deserve good things, and I am working toward them.

blocks.p: Make them yours by changing a word or two until they sound like you.

sections.h2: Tips for keeping an affirmation journal

ul: **Choose believable words.** If an affirmation makes you roll your eyes, soften it.
**Use one a week.** Living with one affirmation for seven days often works better than writing a new one each day.
**Say it out loud.** Reading your affirmation aloud in the morning can help it stick.
**Pair with action.** If your affirmation is I take care of my health, follow it with a glass of water or a short walk.
**Write in the morning.** Try it with our [morning journal prompts](/morning-journal-prompts/).
**Keep it private.** This diary is saved in your browser on this device, with no account.

blocks.p: If faith is part of your life, you can also write prayers and Bible-based encouragement in a [prayer journal](/prayer-journal/) or with [Christian journal prompts](/christian-journal-prompts/). More ideas: [gratitude journal prompts](/gratitude-journal-prompts/) and our full list of [journal prompts](/journal-prompts/).

faq.a: An affirmation journal is a notebook where you write short, positive sentences about yourself, like I can handle hard things, and reflect on why they matter. It is a way of practicing kinder self-talk. Over time, seeing these words in your own writing can help them feel more natural and true.

faq.q: How do I start an affirmation journal?
faq.a: Pick one harsh thought you often have and rewrite it as a kind, believable sentence. Write that affirmation three times, then answer one prompt about why it matters. Read it again in the morning or before a hard moment. Add a new affirmation each week or whenever you need one.

Affirmations tend to help most when they feel believable and are paired with action. Some research suggests positive self-talk can help people feel more confident in stressful moments. They are not magic, and very big statements you do not believe may not help. Start with small, true sentences.

faq.q: How many times should I write an affirmation?
faq.a: There is no set number. Writing an affirmation three to five times is a common habit and only takes a minute. Some people prefer reading one aloud each morning. What matters most is coming back to it often, especially when you need it.

faq.q: What are some affirmation journal examples?
faq.a: Examples include: I can handle one thing at a time. I am allowed to rest. I am learning, and learning takes time. I bring something good to the people around me. The example entry above shows how to turn a harsh thought into a kinder affirmation you can believe.
